battle.name: 卡赫美士戰役
battle.theater: 幼發拉底河西岸卡赫美士
battle.brief: 公元前605年，新巴比倫王尼布甲尼撒二世與米底聯軍在幼發拉底河西岸的卡赫美士擊敗法老尼科二世與亞述殘軍組成的聯軍，埃及退回尼羅河谷，亞述王國就此滅亡，兩河流域的勢力自此直抵地中海東岸。卡牌上的埃及月牙劍早已是王權禮器，當場實戰的是青銅矛、斧、複合弓與輕裝車隊。

kit.name: 埃及月牙劍
kit.history: 外彎的單刃劍，砍下去不用拔。它比直劍更早出現在埃及人的手上。

countries: 交戰的兩邊，是前七世紀末重新瓜分亞述遺產的兩股力量。進攻方是新巴比倫王國與其同盟者米底王國的聯軍：巴比倫一方由國王尼布甲尼撒二世直接指揮，核心是巴比倫城常備的王家步兵，包含持長槍的盾兵、持斧的近戰兵與弓手，配以輕裝車兵與馬匹，軍隊隸屬王室與巴比倫的行政編制，由總督與各區官員分區徵集，並非臨時拼湊的部落兵。拿波那帕爾沙在位時已於前612年攻入尼尼微、前610年取下哈蘭，滅亞述的戰役正是他主持的，這支部隊帶著連年攻城而疲憊卻精銳的經驗，越過幼發拉底河向北作戰。聯軍名單裡的米底軍隊見於後期編年與近現代史家的敘述，編年正文並未留下可核對的記載，其規模與到場時間只能存疑；可以確定的是巴比倫在這一階段需要北方盟友分擔對亞述殘部的壓力。防守方是法老尼科二世治下的埃及第二十六王朝軍隊，加上以卡赫美士為都的亞述殘餘政權：亞述本土淪陷後，其宮廷、人馬與流亡者陸續退到幼發拉底河中游的卡赫美士，與當地阿拉米部眾及埃及其他勢力混居，重新湊成一個聯盟。埃及方面出動的是職業化的王家軍隊，包含善用複合短弓的射手、持長柄青銅矛的步兵、披皮革與金屬鱗片的近衛，以及雙輪輕車的車兵；聯軍中相當一部分是編入埃及傭兵的亞述殘兵與阿拉伯、敘利亞盟軍。雙方實力並非懸殊：埃及軍隊久經沙場，亞述的攻城技術與城防經驗仍在，但亞述已無可用的國家組織與補給體系，只能依賴埃及的支援度日。
countriesEn: The two sides in this conflict were the two powers that were dividing up the ruins of Assyria in the late seventh century BC. On the attacking side stood the Neo-Babylonian kingdom together with its ally Media: the Babylonian contingent was under the direct command of King Nebuchadnezzar II, and its core was the standing infantry of the city of Babylon — shield-bearing spearmen, axe-men and archers — supported by light chariotry and horses; the army belonged to the royal establishment and to the administrative districts of Babylonia, levied by governors and local officials, and was not a hastily assembled tribal force. Nabopolassar had already taken Nineveh in 612 BC and Harran in 610 BC, and the destruction of Assyria was his own work, so this army marched north across the Euphrates with the tired but hard-bitten experience of consecutive campaigns and sieges. The Median troops in the coalition appear in later chronicles and in the narratives of modern historians, while the body of the chronicle itself preserves no detail that can be checked, so their numbers and the timing of their arrival can only remain in doubt; what is certain is that Babylonia needed a northern partner in this phase to share the pressure on the surviving Assyrians. On the defending side were the army of the Egyptian Twenty-Sixth Dynasty under Pharaoh Necho II, together with the rump Assyrian state that had made Carchemish its capital: after the fall of Assyria proper, its court, soldiers and refugees withdrew step by step to Carchemish on the middle Euphrates and mixed with the local Aramaean tribes and other Egyptian-aligned elements, and so a new coalition was put together. Egypt fielded a professional royal army: composite-bow archers, infantry with long bronze-tipped spears, guards clad in leather and scale armour, and light two-wheeled chariots. A considerable part of the coalition consisted of Assyrian survivors and Arab and Syrian auxiliaries taken into Egyptian pay. The two sides were not uneven: the Egyptian army was seasoned, and the Assyrian siegecraft and fortification expertise were still intact, but Assyria no longer possessed a usable state organisation or supply system and could only survive on Egyptian support.
people: 留下姓名的核心人物有三組。第一組是巴比倫王室的父子：拿波那帕爾沙在位時就定下西征之策，公元前605年他在巴比倫城病逝，戰役正好落在他的計劃與他兒子的執行之間；其子尼布甲尼撒二世於同年即位，是這場戰役中真正握有指揮權的人，他後來在耶路撒冷與泰爾留下大量銘文，把自己的勝利一遍遍刻給後世看。第二組是埃及國王尼科二世，即希臘文史料中的 Nechos，公元前609年登基，此前已在北方打了十幾年：前609年他在美吉多擊敗猶大王約西亞，前624年他第一次北上幼發拉底，在卡赫美士被米底與亞述聯軍擊退，十餘年後才再來一次。約瑟夫斯在《古史》第十卷第六節寫這一戰，記法老大敗、營寨被奪、士兵被大量殺傷，殘兵退回埃及。第三組是記錄者與後世的研究者：巴比倫編年史甲本的書吏把「埃及王來到卡赫美士城」寫進王年紀；卡赫美士的破土工作經歷了三代人，1911至1914年由大英博物館的霍加斯主持，並有年輕的勞倫斯參與，1927、1929與1936年由沃利接續發掘，挖出「皇家扶壁」與「水門」一帶的宮殿群，也挖到記錄此役的尼布甲尼撒二世勝利碑。同一批遺址中出土的亞述沙爾馬尼撒三世黑方尖碑，記有「以色列王耶戶進貢」，說明這座城在更早三百年已是東方強權的焦點。
peopleEn: Three groups of people are named in the record. The first is the father and son of the Babylonian royal house: Nabopolassar had settled on the westward campaign himself, and he died of illness in Babylon in 605 BC, so the battle fell precisely between his plan and his son's execution of it. His son Nebuchadnezzar II acceded in the same year and was the man who actually held the command; he later left a large number of inscriptions at Jerusalem and Tyre, carving his victory over and over for posterity. The second is the Egyptian king Necho II, called Nechos in the Greek sources, who took the throne in 609 BC after more than a decade of fighting in the north: in 609 BC he defeated Judah and Josiah of Judah at Megiddo, and in 624 BC he marched north to the Euphrates for the first time and was beaten at Carchemish by the Median and Assyrian coalition, returning to Egypt and coming back only more than ten years later. Josephus, in the sixth section of the tenth book of his Antiquities, describes this battle and records the great defeat of the pharaoh, the seizure of his camp, the slaughter of his soldiers and the retreat of the survivors into Egypt. The third group is made up of the recorders and of later scholars: the scribe of the first Babylonian Chronicle wrote into the regnal annals that the king of Egypt came to the city of Carchemish, and the excavation of Carchemish passed through three generations, beginning with the British Museum's Hogarth in 1911 to 1914, with the young Lawrence among the participants, and continuing under Woolley in 1927, 1929 and 1936, who uncovered the palace group around the Royal Buttress and the Water Gate and also the victory stele of Nebuchadnezzar II recording this very battle. The Black Obelisk of the Assyrian Shalmaneser III, recovered from the same site, records the tribute of Jehu, king of Israel, and shows that this city had already been the focus of Eastern great-power attention three centuries earlier.
kits: 卡牌上的月牙劍，落在這場戰役的時間軸上，幾乎只剩象徵的作用。真正帶有月牙劍形制的青銅短刃，出現在古王國與中王國初期，約公元前二千紀上半葉到前一千七百紀；它外彎的單刃切入人身後不必拔出，握柄窄、背脊厚，適合近身劈砍。進入第二中間期，這種刀在埃及的軍陣中已退場，中王國的墓葬壁畫裡它挂在王室侍從的腰間，與王尾並列，構成「王」字的象形符號，說明它已成為王權的禮器而非作戰的武器；新王國晚期的浮雕又出現外形相近的「鐮刀形劍」，但那是復古的儀仗形制，作為禮器一直留到第二十六王朝，晚期法老在神廟的儀式場面中仍持此類月牙形刀，開羅等地博物館現仍藏有數柄這類青銅月牙劍，刃面帶銅綠，長度多在四十至六十公分之間，可作對照。公元前605年的卡赫美士戰場上，雙方真正攜帶的是別的東西：埃及方面以複合短弓為主要火力，配銅矛、斧、小圓盾與大型皮盾，另有雙輪輕車，車上多由一人操弓、另一人持矛；陣中相當一部分是編入埃及的亞述殘兵，用的是亞述式的長盾、斧與重矛。巴比倫方面以持矛的盾兵為骨幹，輔以銅斧、短劍、弓與皮甲，配有輕車與馬匹，並攜帶圍城用的器材，攻城裝備在後續的阿薩路與提爾戰役中才真正發揮。雙方共有的難題是補給：卡赫美士距巴比倫約八百公里，陸運極慢，糧秣、箭桿、瀝青與飼料多靠幼發拉底河的水運與沿途徵收；埃及軍隊同樣遠離尼羅河，必須依靠當地市鎮的存糧與商隊，攻城器械的木料與繩索則就地砍伐與徵用。
kitsEn: The khopesh on the card, set against the chronology of this battle, survives almost entirely as a symbol. The bronze short blades that truly had the khopesh form appear in the Old Kingdom and the early Middle Kingdom, roughly from the first half of the second millennium BC to around 1700 BC: the outward-curving single edge did not have to be pulled back out of a body, the grip was narrow and the spine thick, which suited close-quarter chopping. During the Second Intermediate Period the knife had already left the Egyptian battle line, and in Middle Kingdom tomb painting it hangs at the waist of the king's attendants beside the royal tail to form the hieroglyph for 'king', which is to say that it had become an attribute of kingship rather than a weapon. Late New Kingdom reliefs show a similar-looking 'sickle-shaped sword', but that is a revival as a ceremonial form, and such blades remained ceremonial down to the Twenty-Sixth Dynasty, where late pharaohs are still shown holding a sickle-shaped knife in temple ritual scenes; several bronze khopeshes of this kind, their blades greened with patina and their length commonly between forty and sixty centimetres, survive in museums such as Cairo and can be used for comparison. What the two sides actually carried at Carchemish in 605 BC was something else. On the Egyptian side the principal missile power was the short composite bow, combined with bronze spears, axes, small round shields and large leather shields, together with light two-wheeled chariots, in which one man commonly handled the bow while another held the spear; a good part of the line consisted of Assyrian survivors enrolled in Egyptian pay, using Assyrian-style long shields, axes and heavy spears. On the Babylonian side the backbone was the spearmen with shields, supported by bronze axes, short swords, bows and leather armour, with light chariots and horses, and with siege equipment carried along, which only came fully into play in the later campaigns against Ashkelon and Tyre. The shared difficulty on both sides was supply: Carchemish lies about eight hundred kilometres from Babylon, land transport was slow, and grain, arrow shafts, bitumen and fodder came mostly by water on the Euphrates or by levy along the line of march; the Egyptian army was equally far from the Nile and had to rely on the stored grain and caravan trade of the local towns, while the timber and rope for the siege machines were cut and requisitioned on the spot.
tactics: 卡赫美士的地形決定了打法。這座城建在幼發拉底河西岸的高地上，東面是河與河岸沙地，北面是灌渠縱橫的農業平原，西面通向敘利亞內陸；城的南北兩端各有一座要塞式的守門，北門即「水門」，與引幼發拉底河水入城的運渠相連。巴比倫軍隊自東岸渡河，選擇在城北較寬的渡段，以船筏與渡橋過江，然後在城北的高地展開成密集的步兵縱隊，把盾牆擺在最前，弓手列於後列；這是典型的新巴比倫攻城戰術，先以盾陣與弓矢消耗守軍，再在火箭與投石掩護下把梯子與攻城器械推上城牆。埃及聯軍的部署則是把主力擺在城外開闊的耕地與渠埂上，步兵正面對住巴比倫人的推進線，弓手與矛手交替掩護，戰車分列兩翼待命；當巴比倫盾兵進入射程，埃及弓手齊射覆蓋其前列，巴比倫軍以投石與弓壓住埃及弓陣，趁其換箭之際縮短距離，以矛與斧近身砍殺。勝負的轉折出現在陣形被突破之後：埃及車兵反衝，企圖裂開巴比倫的正面，卻因己方弓手與前鋒之間失去配合而被分割包圍，巴比倫前鋒自缺口灌入，埃及陣線崩解，軍隊向河與南方的退路上潰散。編年史記埃及王的營寨被奪，約瑟夫斯則記巴比倫人追殺到河邊，屍體塞滿河道，殘部退回埃及。補給線是這一戰的另一條暗線：巴比倫軍靠河運與沿途徵收維持，埃及軍則深入黎凡特內陸數百公里，離開尼羅河與地中海的糧道，攻城與野戰物資都要就地籌措，這一結構性的弱點在潰敗時被放大成全軍瓦解。
tacticsEn: The terrain of Carchemish dictated how the battle was fought. The city stood on high ground on the west bank of the Euphrates: to the east lay the river and its sand flats, to the north the irrigated agricultural plain cut by canals, and to the west the road into the Syrian interior. Fortified gates closed the north and south ends of the town; the northern gate, the Water Gate, was connected to the canal that brought water from the Euphrates into the city. The Babylonian army crossed from the eastern bank at the wider reach north of the city, using boats and pontoon bridges, then deployed on the heights north of the town in dense infantry columns, shields in front and archers behind: this was the standard Neo-Babylonian method of siege, wearing down the defenders with the shield wall and the bow, then pushing ladders and siege machines up to the ramparts under cover of fire and stone-throwers. The Egyptian coalition deployed its strength on the open fields and canal banks outside the city, infantry facing the Babylonian line of advance, archers and spearmen covering one another in turn, chariots held back on the two wings. When the Babylonian shields came within range the Egyptian archers let fly a massed volley over the enemy front, the Babylonians answered with stones and arrows to pin the Egyptian bow line, and in the interval while the Egyptians nocked new arrows they closed the distance and hacked at close quarters with spears and axes. The turning point came once the formation was broken: the Egyptian chariots counter-charged in an attempt to split the Babylonian front, but the loss of coordination between their own archers and their van meant they were cut off and surrounded, the Babylonian spearhead poured through the gap, the Egyptian line disintegrated and the army scattered back towards the river and the southern road. The Chronicle records that the camp of the king of Egypt was taken; Josephus writes that the Babylonians pursued them to the river, the dead filled the watercourse and the survivors withdrew into Egypt. The line of supply was the other hidden thread of this battle: the Babylonian army lived off river transport and levy along the route, while the Egyptian army stood hundreds of kilometres deep in the Syrian interior, far from the grain roads of the Nile and the Mediterranean, and had to find siege and field materials on the spot — a structural weakness that was magnified into the disintegration of the whole army when the line broke.
data: 可核對的數字不多，而且分屬不同層次。時間上，這場戰役的通行紀年是公元前605年；約瑟夫斯把它放在尼布甲尼撒二世在位第一年，巴比倫編年史甲本則記在拿波那帕爾沙第五年或尼布甲尼撒第六年，兩種王年算法相差數年，這就是文獻中另有前604年與前603年兩說的由來。月份上，原始文獻完全沒有記載；依敘利亞戰役通常落在夏收之前、又必須避開幼發拉底河汛期的慣例推斷，多數編年把這一役置於夏季，本條目取六月，並非文獻所載。地理上，卡赫美士在幼發拉底河西岸，約北緯三十六點八度、東經三十八點八度，緊鄰今日土耳其與敘利亞的國界，考古地點為耶拉布魯斯土丘，遺址面積約五十公頃；由此向西到地中海沿岸約一百公里，向東到巴比倫約八百公里，向南到尼羅河三角洲超過四百公里。兵力、陣亡與繳獲，兩部主要文獻都沒有留下數字；能確定的只有結果的方向：埃及王的營寨被奪，其部隊被擊潰。考古與出土物提供了另一組數字：1911至1914年英國博物館主持第一次發掘，1927、1929與1936年沃利主持第二次發掘，挖出「皇家扶壁」「水門」與「鱷魚門」一帶的宮殿與浮雕；記錄此役的尼布甲尼撒二世勝利碑被切成兩塊，殘件分藏大英博物館與安卡拉的安納托利亞文明博物館；同一地點出土的沙爾馬尼撒三世黑方尖碑四面刻滿銘文，是亞述王權的見證。戰後的相關數字可作對照：前597年巴比倫第一次圍攻耶路撒冷，擄走約四千六百四十名居民與官員；前587至586年第二次圍城再擄約三千零二十三人。
dataEn: The verifiable numbers are few, and they belong to different layers. On timing, the accepted date of the battle is 605 BC: Josephus places it in the first year of Nebuchadnezzar II, while the first Babylonian Chronicle enters it under the fifth year of Nabopolassar or the sixth of Nebuchadnezzar; the two regnal-year reckonings differ by several years, and that is the origin of the rival datings of 604 and 603 BC found in the literature. On the month, the original documents preserve nothing at all; by the usual convention that campaigns in Syria fall before the summer harvest and must avoid the flood season of the Euphrates, most chronologies place this battle in the summer, and this entry takes June, which is inference rather than record. Geographically, Carchemish lay on the west bank of the Euphrates at about 36.8 degrees north and 38.8 degrees east, hard against the present frontier of Turkey and Syria; the archaeological site is the mound of Tell Jerablus, roughly fifty hectares in extent. From there it is about a hundred kilometres to the Mediterranean coast, about eight hundred to Babylon, and more than four hundred to the Nile Delta. The numbers of men, losses and booty are given by neither of the two principal sources; all that can be fixed is the direction of the result: the camp of the king of Egypt was taken and his troops broken. Archaeology and the finds supply a second set of figures: the first excavation was run by the British Museum from 1911 to 1914, and the second by Woolley in 1927, 1929 and 1936, uncovering the palaces and reliefs around the Royal Buttress, the Water Gate and the Crocodile Gate; the victory stele of Nebuchadnezzar II that records this battle was cut into two pieces, and the fragments are divided between the British Museum and the Museum of Anatolian Civilizations in Ankara; the Black Obelisk of Shalmaneser III, found at the same spot, carries inscriptions on all four faces and is the standing witness of Assyrian kingship. Figures from the aftermath can be set beside it: in 597 BC Babylonia besieged Jerusalem for the first time and deported about four thousand six hundred and forty residents and officials; in 587 to 586 BC the second siege carried off about three thousand and twenty-three more.
cause: 這場戰爭不是臨時起意，而是前七世紀末亞述崩解的收尾。亞述本土自前612年尼尼微淪陷、前610年哈蘭淪陷之後，其宮廷與軍隊退往幼發拉底河中游的卡赫美士，並以這座城作為北方流亡政權的都城與最後的堡壘。卡赫美士扼住幼發拉底河中游的渡口與通道，是巴比倫通往地中海的咽喉要道；只要它落在亞述與其盟友手上，新巴比倫的西境就永遠被卡住，商隊也不能自由進出腓尼基。埃及的介入同樣有前例：法老尼科二世自公元前609年即位便把手伸進北方的殘局，先在美吉多擊敗猶大與其盟友，前624年又第一次打到卡赫美士，結果被米底與亞述聯軍擊退，軍隊退回埃及。這次失敗並沒有讓他放棄；他花了近二十年重建北方陣線，改與亞述殘部及阿拉米部族結盟，終於在公元前605年捲土重來。對巴比倫而言，開戰還有第二重理由：滅掉亞述的殘餘政權，等於把西部邊界一次推到地中海，兼且切斷埃及與北方反巴比倫勢力的聯合；對米底而言，聯手出兵可避免巴比倫獨佔幼發拉底河中游的轉運權，維持北方的勢力均衡。埃及之所以再度北進，則是因為它不願放棄對腓尼基與黎凡特走廊的控制——那條走廊是埃及穀物、橄欖油與黎凡特銀的市場所在，也是它與北方貿易的門戶；對一個靠尼羅河餘糧支撐的王朝來說，這條走廊的存亡本身就是生存問題。
causeEn: This war was not a sudden outbreak but the closing of the collapse of Assyria in the late seventh century BC. After the fall of Nineveh in 612 BC and of Harran in 610 BC, the Assyrian court and army withdrew to Carchemish on the middle Euphrates and made that city the capital of a northern government in exile and its last fortress. Carchemish held the crossings and the roads of the middle Euphrates; it was the throat of the route from Babylon to the Mediterranean. As long as it remained in the hands of Assyria and its allies, the western frontier of Neo-Babylonia was permanently blocked and its caravans could not move freely into Phoenicia. Egypt's involvement had precedent as well: from his accession in 609 BC Pharaoh Necho II reached into the northern wreckage, defeating Judah and its allies at Megiddo, and in 624 BC marching to Carchemish for the first time, only to be beaten there by the Median and Assyrian coalition and driven back into Egypt. That defeat did not make him give up. He spent nearly twenty years rebuilding the northern front, turned instead to alliance with the surviving Assyrians and the Aramaean tribes, and came back in 605 BC. For Babylonia there was a second reason to fight: to destroy the rump Assyrian state was to push the western frontier to the Mediterranean in a single stroke and to cut Egypt off from any northern coalition against Babylon. For Media, a joint campaign avoided letting Babylonia monopolise the traffic of the middle Euphrates and preserved the balance of power in the north. Egypt marched north again because it would not surrender control of Phoenicia and the Levantine corridor: that corridor was the market for Egyptian grain, olive oil and Levantine silver, and the gateway of its trade with the north, and for a kingdom sustained by the surplus of the Nile the survival of that corridor was itself a question of survival.
impact: 這一仗改寫了整個近東的權力地圖。第一，亞述帝國在制度上正式終結：卡赫美士落入巴比倫之後，亞述王冠再沒有恢復的可能，此後亞述之名只剩一個地理與懷古的名詞。第二，巴比倫的西部邊界推到了地中海，腓尼基的城邦落入新巴比倫的勢力圈，後來尼布甲尼撒二世對泰爾的圍城，即前585至573年那一役，是這一格局的延伸；巴比倫也第一次直接面對地中海貿易的誘惑與麻煩。第三，埃及退回尼羅河谷，失去了對黎凡特的實際控制，尼科二世在國內的威望受損，晚年的注意力轉向三角洲的工程與塞易斯的自強。對猶大而言，麻煩才剛開始：亞述崩解後，猶大在巴比倫與埃及之間動搖，前597年巴比倫第一次圍攻耶路撒冷，擄走王族、官員與工匠，前586年城與聖殿終於被毀；耶利米哀歌把這場敗局寫成「我們的弓已折斷」，正是把卡赫美士的失敗視為整個西亞秩序崩壞的起點之一。第四，軍制上的後果：埃及在失去北方之後加速倚重巴比倫，數代之後塞易斯的薩姆提克一世與阿馬西斯先後與巴比倫聯手對付米底；巴比倫則以這場勝利換來對美索不達米亞與黎凡特的長期壟斷，直到波斯人接管這座城市。考古與學術上，卡赫美士的浮雕、楔形文字泥板與勝利碑，替新亞述與新巴比倫的戰爭藝術、軍服編制與攻城術提供了可見的實物依據，英國博物館的卡赫美士收藏至今仍是這方面的核心材料。
impactEn: This single battle redrew the political map of the Near East. First, the Assyrian empire ended formally as a political institution: once Carchemish fell to Babylonia, the Assyrian crown could never be restored, and from then on Assyria survived only as a geographical and antiquarian name. Second, the western frontier of Babylonia was carried to the Mediterranean, the Phoenician cities fell within its sphere, and the later siege of Tyre by Nebuchadnezzar II in 585 to 573 BC was an extension of that new pattern; Babylonia also faced the temptations and the difficulties of Mediterranean trade for the first time. Third, Egypt fell back into the Nile valley and lost effective control of the Levant; the standing of Necho II at home suffered, and his later attention turned to the works in the Delta and to the self-strengthening of Saïs. For Judah the trouble was only beginning: after the collapse of Assyria, Judah swung between Babylonia and Egypt, and in 597 BC Babylonia besieged Jerusalem for the first time and carried off the royal house, the officials and the craftsmen; in 586 BC the city and the temple were finally destroyed. The Lamentations set the defeat down as 'our bow is broken', treating the loss at Carchemish as one of the opening strokes of the collapse of the whole West Asian order. Fourth, the consequences in military terms: Egypt, having lost the north, leaned harder on Babylonia, and a few generations later the Saite pharaohs Psamtik I and Amasis allied with Babylon against the Medes; Babylonia in turn exchanged this victory for a long monopoly of Mesopotamia and the Levant, until the Persians took over the city. In archaeology and scholarship, the reliefs, cuneiform tablets and victory stele of Carchemish gave the warfare art, the dress and the siegecraft of the Neo-Assyrian and Neo-Babylonian states a visible material basis, and the Carchemish collections of the British Museum remain the core of the evidence.
result: 結果是巴比倫聯軍的決定性勝利，埃及與亞述聯盟在卡赫美士被徹底打散。巴比倫編年史甲本的記載最簡：一支王軍與埃及王在卡赫美士城交戰，埃及王退走，他的營寨被奪，他的部隊被切斷散走。尼布甲尼撒二世為此立碑，碑文宣稱自己渡過幼發拉底河、擊潰埃及軍、屍體塞滿河道，而埃及王帶著殘兵逃回埃及；約瑟夫斯在《古史》裡寫得更具體，說巴比倫軍緊追不放，殺傷甚眾，埃及王才得以收攏殘兵退回尼羅河谷。從軍事的角度說，這是一次殲滅性的會戰加一次成功的追擊：亞述殘餘政權連同其在卡赫美士的城防一起崩解，北方不再有能與巴比倫對抗的獨立軍隊。從政治的角度說，代價卻不輕：新巴比倫在往後十餘年裡連年徵發，編年史多次記下國王下令全國徵兵的消息，財政與民力被這場遠征抽乾，前523年更出現冒充尼布甲尼撒二世的加馬塔起義，前520年前後又有大規模的阿拉米地區叛亂。對埃及而言，這並非終局：它退回淨土後用了兩代時間重建軍力，反而在與米底的戰爭中轉而與巴比倫結盟，於前567年取得對米底的勝利——敵我關係從此反轉，成為六世紀國際關係的一個註腳。史料上也要老實記一筆：這場戰爭沒有留下戰報，沒有留下雙方的兵力數字，最終的勝負要靠巴比倫編年史的片語、尼布甲尼撒的勝利碑與約瑟夫斯的一段敘述拼起來才成立。
resultEn: The result was a decisive victory for the Babylonian coalition, and the Egyptian and Assyrian alliance was completely broken at Carchemish. The first Babylonian Chronicle gives the shortest account: the royal army and the king of Egypt fought at the city of Carchemish, the king of Egypt withdrew, his camp was taken, and his troops were cut off and scattered. Nebuchadnezzar II raised a stele for the occasion, in which he claims that he crossed the Euphrates, broke the Egyptian army, filled the river with the dead, and that the king of Egypt escaped back to Egypt with his survivors. Josephus is more explicit in the Antiquities, writing that the Babylonians pursued closely, inflicted great slaughter, and that only thus did the king of Egypt manage to gather his remnants and withdraw into the Nile valley. Militarily this was an annihilating engagement followed by a successful pursuit: the rump Assyrian state collapsed together with its fortifications at Carchemish, and the north no longer contained an independent army that could stand against Babylonia. Politically, however, the price was heavy: for more than a decade afterwards Neo-Babylonia levied men year after year, the Chronicle records the king's orders for general conscription several times, and the finances and manpower of the country were drained by this distant campaign; in 523 BC there appeared the revolt of Gaumata, who claimed to be Nebuchadnezzar II, and around 520 BC a large rising in the Aramaean districts. For Egypt this was not the end: after falling back to its own territory it rebuilt its army over two generations and, in the war against the Medes, turned instead to alliance with Babylonia, winning the decisive victory over Media in 567 BC — the alignment of enemies and friends had reversed, which is a standing footnote to international relations in the sixth century. The record itself must be handled with care: this campaign left no despatch and no headcount on either side, and the outcome can only be established by piecing together a phrase of the Babylonian Chronicle, the victory stele of Nebuchadnezzar and a passage of Josephus.
